abstract.p: Large Language Models (LLMs) often generate hallucinated content, which is factually incorrect or misleading, posing reliability challenges. The MuSHROOM shared task addresses hallucination detection in multilingual LLM-generated text. This study employs SpanBERT, a transformer model optimized for span-based predictions, to identify hallucinated spans across multiple languages. To address limited training data, we apply dataset augmentation through translation and synthetic generation. The model is evaluated using Intersection over Union (IoU) for span detection and Spearman's correlation for ranking consistency. While the model detects hallucinated spans with moderate accuracy, it struggles with ranking confidence scores. These findings highlight the need for improved probability calibration and multilingual robustness. Future work should refine ranking methods and explore ensemble models for better performance.
